name: MonarchCalendarHeatmap
title: CalendarHeatmap
wrapsNative: A SwiftUI grid of rounded-rectangle days (HStack of VStack weeks in a horizontal ScrollView with defaultScrollAnchor(.trailing) for the year; Grid for the month), the environment Calendar for weeks and names, Date.FormatStyle for dates; inside MonarchChartFrame with the MonarchHeatmap scale and legend and an AXChartDescriptor
summary: Values by day on a calendar grid, a contribution-style year or a month calendar with day numbers, binned into four colour steps with a Less to More legend, today, notes, markers, tap inspection, drill-in and the days as a table.
whenToUse: To show one value per day over weeks or a year (activity, sign-ins, hours logged) so streaks, gaps and busy weeks stand out, or a month where each day opens its details (layout .month).
whenNotToUse: For two arbitrary categories such as weekday by hour use MonarchHeatmap. For a trend where exact values matter use MonarchBarChart or MonarchLineChart. To schedule or show events on dates use a calendar view or the system DatePicker with .graphical.
api: init(_ title: String, days: [MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay], from: Date? = nil, to: Date? = nil, description: String? = nil, layout: MonarchCalendarHeatmapLayout = .year, today: Date? = nil, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, color: MonarchChartColor = .data1, thresholds: [Double]? = nil, showsValues: Bool = true, showsLegend: Bool = true, summary: String? = nil, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, labels: MonarchCalendarHeatmapLabels = MonarchCalendarHeatmapLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay) -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay.init(_ date: Date, value: Double?, valueLabel: String? = nil, note: String? = nil, isInactive: Bool = false, hasMarker: Bool = false)

MonarchCalendarHeatmapLabels.init(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), less: String? = nil, more: String? = nil, noData: String? = nil, rangeBelow: String? = nil, range: String? = nil, rangeAbove: String? = nil, date: String? = nil, value: String? = nil, note: String? = nil, today: String? = nil, dayCountOne: String? = nil, dayCount: String? = nil, summary: String? = nil, highest: String? = nil)

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading.

options.name: days
options.description: One entry per day with something to show: a date, a value (nil for no data), and optional value text, note, non-working flag and marker. Days in the range without an entry are no data; a later entry for the same day wins.

options.name: from
options.description: The first day drawn. The earliest entry when nil.

options.name: to
options.description: The last day drawn. The latest entry when nil.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title, such as the period.

options.name: layout
options.description: year: weeks as columns and weekdays as rows, scrolling sideways; month: a calendar with day numbers and values.

options.name: today
options.description: The day outlined as today. Passed by the app; the component never reads the clock.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error. Ready without an entry in the range shows empty.

options.name: color
options.description: The data colour of the four steps.

options.name: thresholds
options.description: Three ascending values where levels 2, 3 and 4 start. Quarters of the largest value when nil.

options.name: showsValues
options.description: Month layout: writes each day's value text (or note) under its number.

options.name: showsLegend
options.description: Shows the Less to More legend under the grid.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary VoiceOver reads.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the frame's, the legend's, the table headings, Today, the day counts, the summary and the highest day.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values. A number in the environment's locale by default.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the day when it is tapped or selected with VoiceOver; a day without an entry comes with value nil.

states.name: level
states.description: Each day with a value takes one of five fills: the muted background for zero, then the data colour mixed in at 25%, 50%, 75% and 100%.

states.name: no data
states.description: A day in the range without a value is empty with a thin subtle outline.

states.name: non-working
states.description: A day marked isInactive without a value above zero has the subtle background and a dashed outline.

states.name: today
states.description: The day of today has a thick accent outline.

states.name: inspected
states.description: After a tap or a VoiceOver swipe the day has a thick default-text outline and its date, value and note are written under the grid.

states.name: marker
states.description: A day with hasMarker has a small warning-coloured dot in its top trailing corner.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" lists every day with an entry: date, value and, when any day has one, note.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: The frame's placeholder, empty state and error with Try again, at the chart's height.

appearance: Steps mix the chosen data slot into the muted background, as MonarchHeatmap. Days without data use the subtle border colour, non-working days the subtle background with a dashed subtle border, today the accent solid colour, the inspected day the default text colour and markers the warning solid colour ringed with the surface colour. Text is the muted and default text colours, on a surface chip at the two strongest steps. Every colour is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web draws an SVG that shrinks a year to fit the width; on iOS the year keeps 14-point days and scrolls sideways on a phone, opening at the latest week, as planned. Days are Date values read in the environment's Calendar, which also supplies the first weekday (the web's weekStartsOn), the time zone and the weekday and month names; the web takes ISO date strings and a locale. The inspected day is internal state, not a controlled activeDate. There is no keyboard navigation (arrows, Page Up/Down); VoiceOver adjusts day by day in the year and visits each day in the month. Inspection is written under the grid instead of a floating tooltip. Android ships the same MonarchCalendarHeatmap. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry, onSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: Year layout: the grid is one adjustable element named by the generated summary ("181 days from Thu, Jan 1, 2026 to Tue, Jun 30, 2026. Total 812. Highest: …") or summary. Swiping up and down moves one day and its value reads the date, value, note and Today; with onSelect it has the button trait and a double tap selects the day.

Month layout: each day is its own element, labelled with its date and valued with its value, note and Today; it has the selected trait while inspected and the button trait with onSelect. Weekday headings are hidden.
Both layouts carry an AXChartDescriptor with one point per day with a value, for Audio Graphs.
The inspection text under the grid is hidden from VoiceOver because the element already reads it.
The legend is read as its name and its steps.
Zero, no data, non-working days, today and markers differ by fill, outline and dot, and are also in the spoken value and the table, not colour alone.
edgeCases: A range that ends before it starts, or no entries and no range, shows the empty state.
Days are compared by calendar day, so any time of day counts and daylight saving changes do not shift days.
In the year layout days are 14 points, below the 44-point touch target; tapping is a convenience and VoiceOver uses the adjustable element instead.
At the largest text sizes month names and weekday names in the year grid shrink to fit (minimum scale 0.6) and month names are skipped when they would overlap; month cells grow taller.
Tap inspection, horizontal scrolling and Audio Graphs were not tried on a device or with VoiceOver; the grid, styles, text and summary logic are unit-tested.

examples.title: A month of hours with notes and drill-in
examples.code:
MonarchCalendarHeatmap(
    "March 2026",
    days: [
        MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay(day(2), value: 480, valueLabel: "8h"),
        MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay(day(3), value: 0, note: "Missing hours", hasMarker: true),
        MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay(day(7), value: nil, isInactive: true),
        MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay(day(9), value: nil, note: "Holiday", isInactive: true),
        MonarchCalendarHeatmapDay(day(12), value: 600, valueLabel: "10h"),
    ],
    from: day(1),
    to: day(31),
    layout: .month,
    today: day(12),
    color: .data2,
    onSelect: { opened = $0.date }
)
